```{r}
Demand <- read.csv("~/Downloads/SCIF DATA(Articles, Incidence, Population) (1).csv")
```

Modelling the data using negative binomial regression:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)

Demand_Model <- glm.nb(
 Articles ~ Country + Year +
    offset(log(Population)),
  data = Demand
)

summary(Demand_Model)
```

The Australian regression coefficient is 0.671780. This represents the difference in log(publication rate) between AU and US, after adjusting for population size and year. The model is using a log link.

```{r}
exp(0.671780)
```

This means Australia's publication rate is 1.96 times that of the US

Null Hypothesis: There is no difference in publications per capita between AU and US
Alternate Hypothesis: Therer is a significant difference

P-value for CountryAustralia is  <2e-16 *** which is below 0.05. This means the difference is significant. 

CAUTION: This data is only based on the last 7 years. 

```{r, echo=FALSE}

# Plotting the number of publications in AU and US

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(Demand, aes(x = Year, y = Articles,
                   colour = Country,
                   group = Country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Melanoma Mouse-Model Publications",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of publications",
    colour = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

# Calculating the ratio between the two countries
rate <-Demand$Articles[8:14]/Demand$Articles[1:7]
mean(rate)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)

# Using earlier negative binomial model to plot publication rate estimates per capita

library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)

# Creating prediction data
prediction_data <- merge(
  expand.grid(
    Country = c("America", "Australia"),
    Year = 2019:2025
  ),
  transform(
    Demand[c("Country", "Year", "Population")],
    Country = as.character(Country)
  ),
  by = c("Country", "Year")
)

# Predicting publication rates
pred <- predict(Demand_Model, prediction_data, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)

# Calculating rates and 95% confidence intervals per million people
prediction_data <- transform(
  prediction_data,
  Rate  = exp(pred$fit) * 1e6 / Population,
  Lower = exp(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit) * 1000000 / Population,
  Upper = exp(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit) * 1000000 / Population
)

# Plotting the data
ggplot(prediction_data, aes(x = Year, y = Rate, colour = Country)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, fill = Country),
    alpha = 0.2,
    colour = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2019:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Publication Rate Estimates",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Estimated publications (per 1,000,000)",
    colour = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
Demand_Incidence <- read.csv("~/Downloads/SCIF DATA(2019-2023).csv")
library(MASS)
Demand_Incidence_Model <- glm.nb(
  Articles ~ Country + Year + Incidence +
    offset(log(Population)),
  data = Demand_Incidence
)

summary(Demand_Incidence_Model)
exp(1.483511)

# When incidence is included Australia's publication rate is 4.4 times that of the US
# However incidence is has an insignificant impact on no. articles published (p-value 0.060533 > 0.05).
# This specifice analysis is conducted on too small a data set and so is not included in the final deliverable. 

```



```{r, echo = FALSE}
#plotting incidences rates for AU and US
Demand_Historical <- read.csv("~/Downloads/SCIF DATA(AU vs US incidence rate).csv")
ggplot(Demand_Historical, aes(x = Year,
                 y = Incidence.Rate,
                 colour = Country,
                 group = Country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Cancer Incidence Rates: America vs Australia",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Incidence Rate (per 100,000)",
    colour = "Country"
  ) +
 theme_classic() 
```

```{r}
#standard linear model of incidence rates
model <- lm(Incidence.Rate ~ Country + Year, data =  Demand_Historical)
summary(model)
```
P-value for `CountryAustralia` shows significance, supporting that the difference in rates between AU and US is significant.

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", echo = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
# Creating estimated timeline for sourcing mice

# Creating timeline data
activities <- data.frame(
  activity = c(
    "Availability", "Biosecurity", "Shipping",
    "Quarantine", "Acclimatisation", "Rederivation"
  ),
  # Listing start and end times in weeks
  start = c(1, 3, 10, 10.35, 10.35, 10.35),
  end = c(10, 10, 10.35, 14.35, 11.35, 36),
  level = c(3.5, 2.5, 1.5, 3.5, 2.5, 0.5),
  category = c(
    "Live Mice", "Both", "Both",
    "Live Mice", "Live Mice", "Frozen Embryo"
  ))

# Plotting the timeline
ggplot() +

geom_rect(
  data = activities,
  aes(
    xmin = start,
    xmax = end,
    ymin = level - 0.06,
    ymax = level + 0.06,
    fill = category
  )
) + scale_fill_manual(
  name = "Type",
  values = c(
    "Live Mice" = "lightblue",
    "Both" = "lavender",
    "Frozen Embryo" = "pink"
  )
) +
  # Labels
  geom_text(
    data = activities,
    aes(
      x = (start + end) / 2,
      y = level + 0.5,
      label = activity
    ),
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Relative time axis
scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = seq(2, 36, by = 2),
  labels = seq(2, 36, by = 2),
  limits = c(0.1, 36.5)
) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = NULL,
    limits = c(0.1, 6)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sourcing Mice Timeline Estimate",
    x = "Week",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ))
```

```{r}
cost <- read.csv("~/Downloads/SCIF DATA(costs).csv")

# Plotting cost estimates for sourcing mice

# Creating totals data frame
totals <- data.frame(
  Type = c("Embryo", "Live"),
  Total_Cost = c(7251.43, 6124.25)
)

# Creating stacked bar chart
ggplot(cost, aes(x = Type, y = Cost, fill = Expense)) +

  geom_col() +

  # Adding total values above bars
  geom_text(
    data = totals,
    aes(
      x = Type,
      y = Total_Cost,
      label = paste0("$", format(
        round(Total_Cost, 2),
        big.mark = ",",
        nsmall = 2
      ))
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4
  ) +

  # Expense colours
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Initial Cost" = "lightblue",
    "Biosecurity" = "lavender",
    "Freight" = "lightpink"
  )) +

  # Chart labels
  labs(
    title = "Live Mouse vs Frozen Embryo Cost Comparison",
    x = "",
    y = "Cost ($)",
    fill = "Expense"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  # Adding space above bars
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  )

```

```{r}
# Plotting cost estimates with expenses seperate
ggplot(cost, aes(x = Expense, y = Cost, fill = Type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
           width = 0.7) +
scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("Initial Cost", "Biosecurity", "Freight")
)+
  labs(title = "Live Mouse vs Frozen Embryo Cost Comparison",
    x = "Expense Category",
    y = "Cost ($)",
    fill = "Method"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Embryo" = "lightblue",
    "Live" = "lightpink"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() 
```
